reviewers.summary: The round-four changes address the previously reported comment and nested-dictionary lookups. The preflight can still miss valid page content when its dictionary names use PDF #xx escapes, allowing an oversized text source to reach the worker.

findingList.message: Decode PDF name escapes when locating page and content dictionary entries; escaped /Type or /Contents names can bypass the preflight text-source limit.

evidence.codePathTraced: PreflightPageContentSources recognizes pages and their content references by looking up literal /Type and /Contents names. PDF name escapes such as /Ty#70e, /Pa#67e, and /Cont#65nts decode to those same names, but these lookups do not decode them. The scan therefore skips the page and returns without enforcing the text-source limit.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF uses escaped names for its /Type /Page and /Contents entries and references a text stream larger than 524288 bytes. PdfPig resolves the names and reads the stream, while preflight finds no page content and starts the worker without applying the bound. OWASP A04:2025.

reviewers.summary: The updated parser skips comments and nested dictionaries when locating PDF dictionary keys, and the added tests cover the previously reported bypasses. The acceptance criteria’s named behavior tests and CI verification are addressed.
The round-four changes address the previously reported comment and nested-dictionary lookups, but escaped PDF names can still bypass page-content discovery and the text-source bound.

findingList.message: Decode PDF name escapes when locating /Type and /Contents. Escaped names can make preflight skip an oversized page content stream.

evidence.codePathTraced: PreflightPageContentSources recognizes page dictionaries by searching for the literal /Type and /Contents names. PDF names may encode characters with #xx escapes, but FindPdfDictionaryToken compares the raw bytes to the unescaped token.
evidence.failureScenario: An attacker submits a PDF whose page dictionary spells /Type as /#54ype and /Contents as /Con#74ents. PdfPig resolves those names, but preflight skips the page and does not count its oversized text stream; the worker starts without the text-source limit being enforced. OWASP A04:2025.
